"""Partial lexical model: language-sensitive word pieces and delimiters.

Nearby English/Romance function words give a decaying language cue
(roughly eight tokens per half-life), reset at each new document. Long
Latin-script pieces are more negative in Romance contexts, especially shared
Latinate roots and relative-status adjectives. English adjective completions
(proximal, maximal, optimal, temporal) are positive. Several productive suffixes
and simple word classes have weaker offsets. These are group averages, not a
word-by-word lookup; most of the component's smaller lexical variation is lost.
A small rule for 悲 gives a stronger negative response after Japanese kana.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()
ENGLISH = set((
    'the and of to is it that for with as on be are by was this not from '
    'or at an which have has will would their can but'
).split())
ROMANCE = set((
    'de la y e es en da di un per el lo los las del que por para con como '
    'una unos unas más también o os uma dos das não são foi sua seu pela '
    'pelo il gli della delle dei degli che anche alla nel nella sono le '
    'les des du une dans est et pour sur avec aux pas qui vous nous'
).split())
ROOTS = set((
    'activ aplic applic consum contrib declar dimin econom elimin evalu '
    'inform individu utiliz prepar regul relativ vend provinc valor '
    'especific aliment contamin concentr sacrific'
).split())
STATUS = set('superior inferior anterior posterior titular'.split())
ROMANCE_SUFFIXES = set((
    'aciones acion ação ações azione azioni amento amenti imento imenti '
    'iciones ición icion izioni idad idades ativa ativo ativas ativos '
    'ivo iva ivos ivas iore iores ibil ibile ibles'
).split())
SCALAR_ADJECTIVES = set((
    'minimal rapid final prior straight high low large small '
    'potential similar possible'
).split())
LINKING_WORDS = set((
    'thus hence therefore according including within because after'
).split())
TIME_WORDS = set('already never always sometimes often'.split())
SUFFIXES = {
    'able': 0.074,
    'ical': 0.099,
    'ive': -0.027,
    'age': -0.064,
    'ment': -0.021,
    'ity': 0.038,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, english, romance = '', 0.0, 0.0
    else:
        _, previous, english, romance = carry
    english *= 0.92
    romance *= 0.92
    if token[:1].isspace() or not previous or not previous[-1:].isalpha():
        english += word in ENGLISH
        romance += word in ROMANCE
    if any(c in 'áéíóúñàèìòùâêôçãõ' for c in word):
        romance += 0.4
    foreign = max(0.0, (romance - english) / (romance + english + 1.0))
    state = (doc, token, english, romance)

    # These delimiters have distinct, stable responses in training text.
    if token == '<tool_response>': return state, 0.134
    if token == '<tool_call>': return state, 0.089
    if token == '<think>': return state, 0.117
    if token == '</tool_call>': return state, -0.075
    if token in ('<|im_start|>', '<|im_end|>', '<|endoftext|>'):
        return state, 0.017

    value = -0.0015 - 0.01 * foreign
    letters = [c for c in word if c.isalpha()]
    latin = bool(letters) and all(
        'LATIN' in unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in letters
    )
    if latin and len(word) >= 4:
        # Non-vowel endings, except plural s, often leave an uninflected root.
        root_ending = word[-1].isalpha() and word[-1] not in 'aeious'
        value -= (0.065 if root_ending else 0.025) * foreign
    if word.strip('_') in ROOTS:
        value -= 0.037 + 0.36 * foreign
    if word in STATUS:
        value -= 0.017 + 0.47 * foreign
    if token in ROMANCE_SUFFIXES:
        value -= 0.056 + 0.04 * foreign
    if word == 'temporal': value += 0.33 - 0.62 * foreign
    if word == 'maximal': value += 0.27
    if word in SCALAR_ADJECTIVES: value += 0.052
    if word in LINKING_WORDS: value += 0.039
    if word in TIME_WORDS: value += 0.024
    value += SUFFIXES.get(token, 0.0)
    stem = previous.lower()
    if token == 'imal':
        if stem.endswith('prox'): value += 0.60
        elif stem.endswith('max'): value += 0.80
        elif stem.endswith('opt'): value += 0.19
        else: value += 0.072
    if token == 'oral':
        value += 0.61 if stem.endswith('temp') else 0.10
    if token == 'al' and stem.endswith('dist'): value += 0.18
    if token == 'ific': value -= 0.104 + 0.42 * foreign
    if token == '悲':
        japanese = any('\u3040' <= c <= '\u30ff' for c in previous)
        value -= 0.55 if japanese else 0.17
    return state, float(value)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4032 -- a weak "Romance-language context" detector.

What the component does (as far as a short program can say): its activation is
diffuse and mostly token-specific, with a small mean shift by language. Inside
Spanish, Portuguese, French or Italian text it tends to be slightly negative;
in English text it is about zero. Among Romance-looking Latinate word endings
(-ific, -ivo, -ante, -ente, -ament, -aci, -ement, -ción) the negative shift is
larger. The large activations (about +0.6 on "-imal" words such as "proximal"
and "maximal", and about -0.7 on words like " titular") are rare in ordinary text
and are not captured here.

The program tracks, per document, a decayed count of common Romance function
words versus common English function words. When Romance words dominate it
predicts a small negative value (-0.0135, the mean in such text), and a larger
one (-0.08) on Latinate Romance-looking words. Otherwise it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

ROMANCE_WORDS = set(
    "de la que el en los las por con para una un es se del al y o do da dos das "
    "não uma é des le les et est il di che per und".split()
)
ENGLISH_WORDS = set(
    "the of and to is that with for are was this it on as be by from or an which "
    "not have".split()
)
LATIN_ENDINGS = ("ific", "ivo", "ivos", "ante", "ente", "ament", "aci", "ement", "ción", "cion")
ROMANCE_CONTEXT_VALUE = -0.0135
LATINATE_WORD_VALUE = -0.08
DECAY = 0.98


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        carry = (0.0, 0.0)
    romance, english = carry
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    if raw[:1] == " " or len(prefix.token_ids) == 1:
        if word in ROMANCE_WORDS:
            romance += 1
        if word in ENGLISH_WORDS:
            english += 1
    romance *= DECAY
    english *= DECAY
    value = 0.0
    if romance > english + 0.5:
        value = ROMANCE_CONTEXT_VALUE
        if word.isalpha() and word.endswith(LATIN_ENDINGS):
            value = LATINATE_WORD_VALUE
    return (romance, english), value
programs.luna:
"""Predict a small baseline, with a few narrowly guarded lexical exceptions.

The harvested high-impact examples associate “imal” after “prox”, “max”, or
“submax”, and “oral” after “Temp”, with positive activations. A few word tokens
in Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese contexts have negative activations. This
simple rule captures only those examples, not a broad semantic computation.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()
BASELINE = -0.00161


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].casefold()
    previous = ""
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1:
        same_document = prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
        if same_document:
            previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().casefold()

    # In the high-impact examples these suffix tokens complete proximal,
    # maximal/submaximal, or temporal; the left-hand word piece is a useful
    # guard against matching unrelated appearances of the same suffix.
    if token == "imal" and previous in {"prox", "max", "submax"}:
        return None, 0.62
    if token == "oral" and previous == "temp":
        return None, 0.61
    if token.strip() == "titular" and previous in {"el", "algún", "es", ","}:
        return None, -0.69
    if token.strip() == "superior" and previous == "resultado":
        return None, -0.74
    if token == "悲" and previous == "の":
        return None, -0.55
    return None, BASELINE

programs.haiku:
"""Degree detector for layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4033.

What it does: this component fires on the concept "degree" wherever it appears in text.
The strongest responses are the English word "degree"/"degrees" (angles, temperatures,
academic degrees, "to a degree") and the degree sign ° (also º and ˚). Weaker responses
come from the CJK word 度 (degree), 程度 (extent, degree), 学位 (academic degree),
"deg" fragments, the unit abbreviations °C and °F, and the word "extent". The word "of"
right after "degree" ("degree of freedom") also responds, moderately, and so do superscript
square/cube marks (², ³, ¹), a weaker cousin of the degree sign.
Everything else predicts 0; the component's small diffuse noise is not modelled.

Values are typical activations (in the component's own units) read off the training rows.
"""

READS = ()

DEGREE_WORDS = {"degree", "degrees"}          # English word, any case
SYMBOLS = {"°": 4.7, "º": 3.8, "˚": 2.7}      # degree signs
SIGNS = {"°C": 1.8, "°F": 1.6}                # Celsius / Fahrenheit
DEGREE_ALSO = {"度": 1.5, "程度": 1.3, "学位": 3.0, "deg": 2.1, "extent": 1.3}
SUPERSCRIPTS = {"²": 0.4, "³": 0.6, "¹": 0.7}  # squared / cubed / first-power marks


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    word = raw.lower()
    if word in DEGREE_WORDS:
        return carry, 5.0
    if raw in SYMBOLS:
        return carry, SYMBOLS[raw]
    if raw in SIGNS:
        return carry, SIGNS[raw]
    if raw in DEGREE_ALSO:
        return carry, DEGREE_ALSO[raw]
    if raw in SUPERSCRIPTS:
        return carry, SUPERSCRIPTS[raw]
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if word == "of" and same_doc and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() in DEGREE_WORDS:
        return carry, 2.7
    return carry, 0.0

"""A partial lexical approximation, not a single-topic detector.

Chinese cultivation, swords and calamity have strong negative responses.
English responses are weaker and mixed: possibility/approximation is positive,
while universal quantification, comparison and knowing are negative. These
word-class averages miss much of the component's token-specific variation.
A few phrase and document-start adjustments use the immediately prior token.
"""
READS = ()

# Named word classes, with training-average activations.
WORD_CLASSES = (
    ('universal quantification', -.077, 'every everyone everybody always overall'),
    ('comparison', -.048, 'better best higher high same similar'),
    ('novelty and age', -.034, 'new young fresh old'),
    ('knowing', -.056, 'know known knows knowing knowledge understand understanding'),
    ('liberty', -.075, 'free freedom freely'),
    ('community and service', -.063, 'community service'),
    ('location', -.047, 'located place places location'),
    ('significance and variety', -.041, 'important various such'),
    ('ignoring', -.070, 'ignore ignored ignores ignoring'),
    ('uniqueness', -.076, 'unique exclusive'),
    ('music', -.075, 'music musical'),
    ('ceremonies', -.105, 'marriage wedding ceremony dinner'),
    ('seasonal weather', -.093, 'summer winter snow'),
    ('training', -.080, 'training'),
    ('online', -.081, 'online'),
    ('half', -.081, 'half'),
    ('possibility', .040, 'may might could'),
    ('approximation', .085, 'almost nearly quite rather'),
    ('frequency', .054, 'often once sometimes'),
    ('alternative', .070, 'either neither'),
    ('pair', -.045, 'both'),
    ('care and emphasis', .101, 'carefully seriously strongly primarily partially'),
    ('assertion', .086, 'assert asserts assertion'),
    ('details', .076, 'details detail'),
    ('interior', .041, 'into inside within'),
    ('exterior', -.036, 'out outside'),
    ('vertical position', -.047, 'under above below behind'),
    ('crossing and proximity', .060, 'across near along'),
    ('source and comparison', .022, 'from than'),
    ('possessive determiners', -.025, 'its their'),
    ('third-person plural', .030, 'they'),
)
WORD_VALUE = {word: value for _, value, words in WORD_CLASSES
              for word in words.split()}

# Separate roots from whole words: their response magnitudes differ greatly.
CHINESE_CLASSES = (
    ('cultivation', -.85, '修炼 修煉 修为 修為'),
    ('internal power', -.60, '功力 武功'),
    ('swords', -.49, '剑 劍'),
    ('calamity', -.50, '劫'),
    ('martial-arts world', -.46, '江湖 掌门 掌門'),
    ('refining', -.34, '炼 煉'),
    ('all', -.34, '皆'),
    ('surprise', -.33, '竟 竟然 居然 果然'),
    ('martial prowess', -.28, '实力 實力 高手 招'),
    ('spiritual roots', -.12, '修 仙 丹 风水 風水'),
    ('way and method', -.08, '道 法'),
    ('mind and breath', -.08, '心 气 氣 精神'),
)
WORD_VALUE.update({word: value for _, value, words in CHINESE_CLASSES
                   for word in words.split()})
LINKING_WORDS = frozenset('a an the of to and or but in on for with'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().lower()
    old = previous.strip().lower()
    value = WORD_VALUE.get(word, 0.0)

    # Small orthographic baselines.
    if any('\u4e00' <= c <= '\u9fff' for c in text) and word not in WORD_VALUE:
        value += .016 - .010 * min(len(word), 4)
    if '\ufffd' in text:
        value += .009
    if not word and '\n' in text and text.startswith(' '):
        value -= .017
    if text == '\r':
        value -= .13
    if text in {"'s", '’s'}:
        value += .021
    if word in {'6', '8'}:
        value -= .010
    if word == '</think>':
        value = -.083
    elif word == '</tool_call>':
        value = .095
    if word and not any(c.isalnum() for c in word):
        if '&' in word:
            value += .030
        if '_' in word:
            value += .013
        if '!' in word or '！' in word:
            value -= .017

    # Familiar phrases have different responses from the word alone.
    if word == 'of':
        if old in {'lot', 'majority', 'bunch'}:
            value += .085
        elif old == 'number':
            value -= .040
        elif old in {'use', 'type', 'kind', 'view', 'set', 'terms',
                     'concept', 'expression'}:
            value -= .053
        elif old in {'vicinity', 'intersection', 'presence', 'involvement'}:
            value += .085
    elif word == 'to':
        if old in {'get', 'got', 'prone', 'easy', 'equal', 'adjacent'}:
            value += .072
        elif old in {'try', 'need', 'want', 'failed', 'decided', 'love', 'like'}:
            value -= .037
    elif word == 'you' and old in {'if', 'when', 'can', 'do', 'did', 'would'}:
        value += .054
    elif word == 'with' and old in {'compatible', 'incompatible', 'consistent'}:
        value += .080
    elif word == 'up' and old in {'pick', 'picked', 'picking'}:
        value += .090
    elif word == '法' and old == '功':
        value = -.85

    # A secondary response to data-change callback names.
    if word == 'ondatachange':
        value = .60
    elif word in {'valueeventlistener', 'datasnapshot'}:
        value = .22
    elif word == 'snapshot' and old.endswith('data'):
        value = .20

    if first:
        value += .017
        if word in LINKING_WORDS:
            value += .037
        if word == '#':
            value += .20
    return (doc, text), float(value)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4034 -- a weak, mostly-silent component.

What it does, in plain terms: it is a token-level feature that goes negative on
Chinese cultivation / wuxia-novel vocabulary (修炼 "cultivate", 修为 "cultivation
attainment", 修士 "cultivator", 功力 "skill/power", 劫 "tribulation", 皆 "all",
仙 "immortal", 大道 "the Great Way", 剑 "sword"). Its activation is small everywhere
else, and no coarse rule (script, digits, punctuation, position) captures the rest.

This program predicts about -0.13 on those words and 0 on every other token. It is
the one readable concept we found; it explains only about 0.2% of the activation's
variance, so it is a sketch of the component's sign, not a full account of it.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

CULTIVATION = frozenset(
    ["修炼", "修为", "修士", "修", "修道", "功力", "劫", "渡劫", "皆", "仙", "大道",
     "剑", "化解", "灵力", "法力", "金丹", "元婴", "筑基", "飞升", "境界", "神识"]
)
VALUE = -0.13


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # Stateless: each token is judged alone, so document boundaries need no handling.
    return None, VALUE if prefix.token_strings[-1] in CULTIVATION else 0.0

"""Activation of a 'use / employ' detector (layer-0 MLP unit).

What it does: the unit lights up on words meaning "to use, employ or utilize
something": use, used, using, uses, utilize, employ, leverage, misuse, and the
same idea in other languages (用 / 使用 / 利用 / 运用, использовать, 사용,
استخدام, ใช้, usar). It is weaker on near-synonyms about putting something to
work (apply, handle, manage, navigate, incorporate, manipulate). It also fires on
the preposition right after a use-noun ("the use OF") and on "with" after
"interact". Everywhere else it is about zero. The program only looks at the
current token and the one before it, so it is causal by construction.
"""

READS = ()

# Words for using / employing something, with their typical strength.
USE_WORDS = {
    "use": 0.8, "uses": 0.8, "used": 0.8, "using": 0.6, "usage": 0.5, "misuse": 1.1,
    "utilize": 0.9, "utilized": 1.1, "utilizing": 1.1, "utilise": 0.9,
    "employ": 0.8, "employs": 0.9, "employed": 0.8, "employing": 0.8,
    "leverage": 1.2,
    "用": 0.8, "使用": 0.6, "利用": 0.8, "运用": 1.4,
    "사용": 0.6, "استخدام": 0.6, "ใช้": 0.8, "ご利用": 0.65, "usar": 0.4, "uso": 0.6,
}
# Near-synonyms: putting something to work, weaker.
NEAR_USE = {
    "apply": 0.25, "applied": 0.25, "applying": 0.25, "applies": 0.25,
    "handle": 0.3, "handles": 0.35, "handled": 0.25,
    "manage": 0.35, "manages": 0.4, "managed": 0.2, "managing": 0.45,
    "navigate": 0.6, "incorporate": 0.4, "incorporated": 0.3, "incorporating": 0.5,
    "manipulate": 0.4, "abuse": 0.5, "lever": 0.5, "combining": 0.25,
}
# Nouns after which "of" lights up: "the use of", "application of", ...
USE_NOUNS = {"use", "usage", "application", "abuse", "integration", "interaction",
             "power", "management", "combination", "utilization", "misuse"}
INTERACT = {"interact", "interacts", "interacting", "interaction"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    # the previous token counts only inside the same document
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""

    if word.startswith("использ"):  # Russian "использовать" and forms
        return None, 0.8
    value = USE_WORDS.get(word, NEAR_USE.get(word, 0.0))
    if value:
        return None, float(value)
    if word == "of" and prev in USE_NOUNS:
        return None, 1.0 if prev in ("use", "using", "used", "uses") else 0.4
    if word == "with" and prev in INTERACT:
        return None, 0.6
    return None, 0.0

programs.haiku:
"""Bare space right after a comma: the slot where a number is about to start.

Qwen splits digits into single tokens, and the space before a number becomes its own
bare " " token. So in "born March 21, 1993", "(2016), 40" or "Vol. 4, 1994" the
component goes strongly negative on that bare " " when it directly follows a comma.
It is somewhat less negative after another comma-ending token ("),", ".,", '",')
and on a literal backslash after a comma (escaped "\\n" in code strings). It also
dips negative on the first digit after ", ". Everywhere else it is near zero.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    cur = tokens[-1]
    same_doc = len(tokens) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = tokens[-2] if same_doc else ""
    before = tokens[-3] if len(tokens) > 2 and same_doc and prefix.document_ids[-3] == prefix.document_ids[-1] else ""
    if cur == " " and prev == ",":
        return carry, -2.9
    if cur == " " and prev.endswith(","):
        return carry, -2.5
    if cur == " " and prev.endswith(";"):
        return carry, -0.8
    if cur == "\\" and prev.endswith(","):
        return carry, -1.7
    if cur.isdigit() and prev == " " and before.endswith(","):
        return carry, -0.6
    return carry, 0.0

    (-1.4, 'being coming having becoming talking asking referring saying telling'),
    (-1.65, 'able unable capable sure afraid'),  # Ability and certainty.
    (-1.05, 'interested concerned glad sorry aware willing grateful worried '

    (-0.75, 'true right wrong clear unclear fine ready worth careful confident due'),
    (-0.4, 'possible impossible important necessary responsible likely correct '
     'safe okay useful helpful easy good available'),
    (-0.55, 'done born told meant based expected designed asked supposed '
     'met tasked'),
    (-1.25, 'been gonna'),
    (-0.75, 'really'),

              'very quite clearly actually often probably'.split()) | {"'t"}

                 'during according interesting amazing confusing conflicting '
                 'exciting fascinating misleading challenging disappointing '
                 'frustrating outstanding existing'.split())
SUFFIXES = set('ing ting ating izing ising ling'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    fresh = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    _, previous, cue, previous_cue = (doc, '', 0.0, 0.0) if fresh else carry
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]

            value -= 0.2 + 0.15 * previous_cue

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection, component 4039: "predicate after a form of BE".

What it does: this component goes negative on the word that completes a
be-verb phrase. Its strongest responses are
  * a progressive verb after be ("I'm looking", "is talking", "are focusing"): about -1.0
  * a be + sure/able/unable/unsure ("I'm sure", "was unable", "will be able"): about -1.25
  * "to" after going/came/comes ("it's going to", "were going to"): about -0.75
Adverbs may sit between the be-form and the predicate ("are already working",
"are not getting"). Everything else, including a be-form followed by an article,
adjective or noun ("is a", "are different"), gives 0. The magnitudes are scaled
so the predictions roughly match the component's size.

How it is read: the prefix is scanned backwards from the current token, skipping
adverbs, to find the nearest word. If that word is a form of "be" (and both tokens
are in the same document), the current token is scored by the rules above.
"""

READS = ()

BE = {"am", "is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "being",
      "'m", "'re", "'s", "’m", "’re", "’s"}
ADV = {"not", "still", "already", "also", "clearly", "hugely", "just",
       "really", "very", "all", "now"}
SURE = {"sure", "able", "unable", "unsure"}
MOTION = {"going", "looking", "came", "comes", "come", "went"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = [t.strip().lower() for t in prefix.token_strings]
    cur = toks[-1]
    if len(toks) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    # walk back over adverbs to the word that the current token follows
    j = len(toks) - 2
    while j > 0 and toks[j] in ADV:
        j -= 1
    if cur == "to" and toks[j] in MOTION and j > 0 and toks[j - 1] in BE:
        return None, -0.75  # "going to" in a be-phrase
    if toks[j] not in BE or not cur.isalpha():
        return None, 0.0
    if cur in SURE:
        return None, -1.25  # "be sure / able / unable"
    if cur.endswith("ing"):
        return None, -1.0  # progressive: "be looking / talking / doing"
    return None, 0.0

    (-0.192, -0.478),  # four

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4072 - a "p-then-next-piece" detector.

The component is quiet on most tokens. It speaks up on the second piece of a word that is
split right after a piece ending in the letter p (or its Cyrillic/Greek look-alikes п, π):
"op|f", "Zop|f", "p|err", "Eup|hr", "P|fe", "nep|ř".  What it outputs depends on the
first letter of that second piece:

  * h-sound (h)                        -> strongly negative  (pH, Eup|hr, gep|hy)
  * r- or f-sound (r, р, f, ф, ř, ρ)   -> positive           (Zop|f, p|fl, nep|ř)
  * a vowel                            -> slightly positive
  * t/k/s/c-sound                      -> slightly negative
  * anything else, or no p before it   -> 0

"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

P_ENDINGS = "pпπ"                       # a previous piece ending in one of these
STRONG_NEGATIVE = "h"                   # h after p: pH, Eup|hr
POSITIVE = "rрfфřρ"                     # r- and f-sounds after p
VOWELS = "aeiouyаеиоуыэюяäöüáéíóúàèâêôā"
WEAK_NEGATIVE = "tтτсцk"                # t-, s-, c-, k-sounds after p


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    # The current piece must continue a word: a letter, with no space before it.
    if not word or not word[0].isalpha() or not before or before[-1].lower() not in P_ENDINGS:

    first = word[0].lower()
    if first in STRONG_NEGATIVE:
        value = -2.5
    elif first in POSITIVE:
        value = 1.0
    elif first in VOWELS:
        value = 0.2
    elif first in WEAK_NEGATIVE:
        value = -0.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Detect A-like onsets in the middle of a word.

Short a-initial fragments after consonants are positive. Longer fragments
and vowels in the preceding fragment dilute this response. Nasals/liquids
before the a weaken it; voiced stops and voiceless nonsibilant fricatives
strengthen it. An ensuing n strengthens it, while s or t weaken it.
At vowel and punctuation boundaries the response is usually negative.
Capitalization and a diacritic other than acute/grave also attenuate it.

import unicodedata

READS = ()
VOWELS = frozenset('aeiouаеёиоуыэюяαεηιουωاوي')
A_LIKE = frozenset('aаαاա')
ALPHABETS = ('LATIN', 'CYRILLIC', 'GREEK', 'ARABIC', 'ARMENIAN')
SONORANTS = frozenset('mnlrwyмнлрй')
VOICED_STOPS = frozenset('bdgбдг')
VOICELESS_NONSIBILANT_FRICATIVES = frozenset('fhфх')


def base_letters(text):
    return ''.join(unicodedata.normalize('NFD', c.lower())[0] for c in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    before = base_letters(previous)
    last = before[-1:]
    alphabetic = bool(last) and unicodedata.name(last, '').startswith(ALPHABETS)
    consonant = alphabetic and last.isalpha() and last not in VOWELS
    value = -0.012 if token.isalpha() and consonant else 0.0
    letters = base_letters(token)
    if token and token.isalpha() and letters[0] in A_LIKE:
        n = len(token)
        if consonant:
            strength = 0.71 + 0.11 * (n == 1)
            strength += 0.09 * previous[-1:].isupper()
            if token[0].isupper():
                strength -= 0.14 if n > 1 and token.isupper() else 0.37
            if letters[0] == 'a' and token[0].lower() not in 'aáà':
                strength -= 0.44
            if last in SONORANTS:
                strength -= 0.10
            elif last in VOICED_STOPS:
                strength += 0.22
            elif last in VOICELESS_NONSIBILANT_FRICATIVES:
                strength += 0.25
            if letters[1:2] in ('n', 'н'):
                strength += 0.14
            elif letters[1:2] in ('s', 't', 'с', 'т'):
                strength -= 0.10
            decay = 0.28 * max(n - 2, 0)
            decay += 0.10 * min(max(len(previous.strip()) - 1, 0), 12)
            decay += 0.35 * sum(c in VOWELS for c in before)
            value = strength * math.exp(-decay)
        elif not previous:
            value = 0.024 if n == 1 else 0.21 * math.exp(-0.5 * (n - 2))
        elif last in VOWELS:
            value = 0.104 if n == 1 else -0.118 * math.exp(-0.35 * (n - 2))
        elif last.isdigit():
            value = 0.094 if n == 1 else -0.080 * math.exp(-0.7 * (n - 2))
        elif last.isalpha():
            value = 0.0  # Unmodeled writing systems, e.g. preceding ideographs.
        else:
            value = -0.038 if n == 1 else -0.188 * math.exp(-0.35 * (n - 2))
    return (doc, token), float(value)
